findings.title: Assert used for runtime type check in production code
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit contains `assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)` as a runtime type guard. Asserts are stripped under `python -O`, which is used by some production images and packaging tools. If the assumption is ever violated (e.g., an upstream change delivers a non-BrokerValue message.value), the code will silently fall into the broad `except Exception` block, the message will be marked complete and committed without ever being processed (data loss). Use an explicit `if not isinstance(...):` check and either drop via DLQ or raise.

findings.title: Submit error path silently drops messages and commits their offsets
findings.body: The broad `except Exception` in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches any failure during decoding, building the WorkItem, invoking `grouping_fn`, or calling `queue_pool.submit`. When caught, it calls `offset_tracker.add_offset(...)` followed immediately by `complete_offset(...)`. Because the offset is now present in `all_offsets` and absent from `outstanding`, the commit loop treats it as fully processed and calls `commit_function({partition: offset})`. The Kafka offset advances, the message is never queued, and the work item is permanently lost with only a `logger.exception` line as evidence. This is broader than the explicit `if result is None:` path (which mirrors existing decode-failure behavior) and will silently drop messages on any bug in user-provided code (e.g. `grouping_fn`). At minimum, the message should be routed to the DLQ, or the exception should be re-raised to crash the consumer and force investigation. Note that `uptime-results` is configured without a `dlq_topic` in `KAFKA_CONSUMERS`, so there is no DLQ to send to; this should be addressed before relying on the mode.

findings.title: Sentry transaction name uses 'monitors.' prefix for the uptime consumer
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run names its Sentry transaction `f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}"`. This consumer is registered for `Topic.UPTIME_RESULTS` (see `sentry.consumers.KAFKA_CONSUMERS["uptime-results"]` and the UptimeResultsStrategyFactory subclass), so the prefix should be `uptime.` (or some neutral identifier). The same incorrect `monitors.` prefix is used by the existing code in `result_consumer.py:49`, which is why it likely got copy-pasted here; the new transaction should be fixed so traces and performance dashboards for this consumer are correctly grouped. ResultProcessor's transaction (result_consumer.py:49) has the same problem and was inherited by this PR through the new processing path.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts the opposite of its docstring
findings.body: Inside `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, two messages are submitted (offsets 100 and 101) and the first is configured to raise. The OrderedQueueWorker catches the exception, logs it, and still calls `complete_offset` for both, so the commit loop will commit offset 101 (last processed). However the test ends with `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which asserts that NO commits happen for the partition. This contradicts the docstring ("errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages") and means the test passes whether or not the desired behavior is implemented. The assertion should be the opposite, e.g. `assert test_partition in committed_offsets` and `assert committed_offsets[test_partition] == 102` (101 + 1, mirroring the +1 in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker.commit_offsets`).

findings.title: --mode help text still describes only 'parallel uses multithreading'
findings.body: The `uptime_options()` click choices were extended to include `thread-queue-parallel` but the help string still reads `"The mode to process results in. Parallel uses multithreading."`. Operators picking a mode from `--help` have no indication that the new option exists or what it does. Either update the help text to enumerate the modes (and describe what `thread-queue-parallel` does) or remove the now-misleading sentence about parallel using multithreading.

findings.title: Docstring claims consistent group→queue assignment, but hash() is process-randomized
findings.body: FixedQueuePool's docstring promises "Each group is consistently assigned to the same queue" and `get_queue_for_group` is implemented as `return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`. CPython randomizes the string hash seed per process unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is fixed, so two runs of the consumer can map the same group to different queues. The test `test_consistent_group_assignment` only checks within a single process, so the cross-process case is not covered. In practice ordering survives because Kafka's per-partition order pins messages to one partition and that partition's items all map to one queue within a single process — but the docstring's literal claim is false and will mislead anyone reasoning about the code. Either use a stable hash (e.g. `hashlib.blake2b(group_key, ...).digest()` mod num_queues) or correct the docstring to describe the actual guarantee.

findings.title: WorkItem.message field is written but never read
findings.body: `WorkItem.message` is set by `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` when constructing the work item, but no code path ever reads it (the worker only accesses `work_item.partition`, `work_item.offset`, and `work_item.result`). Either it should be used (e.g. for DLQ routing on exception, or for re-injecting on retry) or it should be removed from the dataclass to avoid carrying a dead reference to the original Message.

findings.title: test_concurrent_processing_across_groups does not actually verify concurrency
findings.body: The test submits 6 items split across 3 group_keys and asserts that `groups_seen` ends up with 3 distinct groups in `processed_items`. This would pass even if all 6 items were processed sequentially in a single worker (the test only checks that all groups were visited, not that they were visited in parallel). To genuinely test concurrency, the result_processor should record the timestamps (or an overlap window) at which it starts processing each item and assert that items for different groups were processed simultaneously, or use a thread-aware assertion such as verifying that processing started for at least two different groups before any single item completed.
